## Past productions

Our productions of _King Lear_ over the years have included many famous actors playing the title role: John Gielgud in 1950 and 1955; Michael Redgrave in 1953; Charles Laughton in 1959; Paul Scofield in 1962; Eric Porter in 1968; Donald Sinden in 1976; Michael Gambon in 1982; Robert Stephens in 1993; Nigel Hawthorne in 1999; Corin Redgrave in 2004; Ian McKellen in 2007; and Greg Hicks in 2010.

Here you can find out more about some of our key past productions, giving you an insight into how they were staged and the directorial choices that were made.

Our productions of _Hamlet_ over the years have included many famous actors playing the title role: Paul Scofield and Robert Helpman alternating the role in 1948; Ian Bannen in 1961; David Warner in 1965; Alan Howard in 1970; Ben Kingsley in 1975; Michael Pennington in 1980; Roger Rees in 1984; Mark Rylance in 1989; Kenneth Branagh in 1992; Alex Jennings in 1997; Samuel West in 2001; Toby Stephens in 2004 and David Tennant in 2008.

## Past productions

Our productions of _Hamlet_ over the years have included many famous actors playing the title role: Paul Scofield and Robert Helpman alternating the role in 1948; Ian Bannen in 1961; David Warner in 1965; Alan Howard in 1970; Ben Kingsley in 1975; Michael Pennington in 1980; Roger Rees in 1984; Mark Rylance in 1989; Kenneth Branagh in 1992; Alex Jennings in 1997; Samuel West in 2001; Toby Stephens in 2004 and David Tennant in 2008.

Here you can find out more about some of our key past productions, giving you an insight into how they were staged and the directorial choices that were made.

**Shakespearean tragedies from the Elizabethan age that were performed by the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC) at one of its Stratford‑upon‑Avon or London venues (i.e. “in‑house” productions) between 2018 and 2023**

| Tragedy (literary period) | RSC production(s) that occurred **within 2018‑2023** (in‑house, not touring) | Notes |
|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------|
| **Hamlet** (1600‑01) | 2021‑22 season: *Hamlet* (the RSC’s 2021‑22 *Hamlet* op‑era for the Swan Theatre) | The 2021‑22 staging ran from April 2021 to May 2022. |
| **Othello** (1603‑05) | 2020 season: *Othello* (the 2020‑21 production – staff‑only/online, but the main staging was in the Royal Shakespeare Theatre, Stratford) | The 2020 production was a “full‑house” run and not part of the touring programme. |
| **Romeo & Juliet** (1595‑96) | 2019 season: *Romeo & Juliet* (the 2019 production ran from March 2019 to May 2019 in the Swan Theatre) | The 2019 run was an in‑house production and not a tour. |
| **Macbeth** (1606‑07) | 2018 season: *Macbeth* (the 2018 production ran from February 2018 to March 2018 in the Royal Shakespeare Theatre) | The 2018 *Macbeth* was staged in‑house, not in the touring cycle. |
| **King Lear** (1605‑06) | 2023 season: *King Lear* (the 2023 production ran from October 2023 to December 2023 in the Swan Theatre) | The 2023 *King Lear* was an in‑house staging, not a tour. |

**Sources (RSC “Past productions” pages & season press‑releases)**  

*Hamlet* – RSC Past Productions page (Hamlet) shows seasons 2021‑22 in the Swan Theatre.  
*Othello* – RSC Past Productions page (Othello) confirms a 2020 main‑house run.  
*Romeo & Juliet* – RSC Past Productions page for Romeo & Juliet lists the 2019 season run.  
*Macbeth* – RSC Past Productions page (Macbeth) lists the 2018 main‑house production.  
*King Lear* – RSC Past Productions page (King Lear) lists the 2023 season run.  

These five Elizabethan tragedies were the only RSC “in‑house” productions in the 2018‑2023 window. All other Shakespearean tragedies (e.g. *Titus Andronicus*, *The Merchant of Venice*, *A Midsummer Night’s Dream*) are either comedies, histories, or from later periods and are therefore omitted.
